literal: A clansman of Yu named Zhongrang was Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing in the Tianbao era.
idiomatic: Yu had a kinsman, Zhongrang, who served as left vice director of the masters of writing in the Tianbao era.

literal: Zhu Cai, styled Daiwen, was a man of the Wu capital.
idiomatic: Zhu Cai, styled Daiwen, came from the Wu capital.

literal: When Xiao Zhuang was at Huainan, he made Cai concurrently irregular attendant of the scattered cavalry and sent him as deputy to Yuan Shuang on a mission to court.
idiomatic: While Xiao Zhuang held Huainan, he gave Cai the concurrent post of irregular attendant of the scattered cavalry and sent him as Yuan Shuang's deputy on a mission to court.

literal: When Zhuang was defeated, Cai remained at Ye.
idiomatic: When Zhuang fell, Cai stayed behind at Ye.

literal: He was gradually promoted to doctorate of the National University and remonstrance and review grandee.
idiomatic: He rose by degrees to doctorate of the National University and remonstrance and review grandee.

literal: When Qi fell, he traveled as a guest in Xindu and died there.
idiomatic: After Qi fell he wandered as a guest in Xindu and died there.

literal: Xun Zhongju, styled Shigao, was a man of Yingchuan whose family had long dwelt south of the Yangzi.
idiomatic: Xun Zhongju, styled Shigao, was from Yingchuan; his house had lived for generations in the lands south of the Yangzi.

literal: In Liang service he was magistrate of Nansha; following Xiao Ming at Hanshan he was taken prisoner.
idiomatic: Under Liang he was magistrate of Nansha; he followed Xiao Ming to Hanshan and was taken prisoner.

literal: Prince Changle Wei Can treated him with great courtesy.
idiomatic: Prince Changle Wei Can honored him deeply.

literal: Drinking heavily with Can, he bit Can's finger down to the bone.
idiomatic: Once, drinking hard with Can, he bit Can's finger to the bone.

literal: When Xianzu learned of it, he had Zhongju beaten one hundred strokes with the stick.
idiomatic: Xianzu heard of it and had Zhongju beaten one hundred strokes.

literal: When someone asked the reason, he answered: "How was I to know? I must have mistaken it for a fly-whisk handle.
idiomatic: Asked why, he said, "How was I to know? I must have taken it for the handle of a fly-whisk.

literal: " He entered the hall and was appointed gentleman of seals and credentials.
idiomatic: " He entered the Forest of Literature Hall and was made gentleman of seals and credentials.

literal: Later, because he was old and his household poor, he was sent out as grand administrator of Yining.
idiomatic: Later, old age and poverty at home sent him out as grand administrator of Yining.

literal: Zhongju and Li Gai of Zhao commandery were close friends; when Gai died, Zhongju went to his house and composed a pentasyllabic poem in sixteen rhyme-groups to mourn him—the words were deeply sorrowful.
idiomatic: Zhongju and Li Gai of Zhao were close friends; when Gai died, Zhongju went to his house and wrote a pentasyllabic poem in sixteen rhyme-groups to mourn him—its language was piercingly sad.

literal: The age praised its beauty.
idiomatic: His age praised its beauty.

literal: Xiao Min, styled Renzu, was son of Marquis Ye of Shanghuang in Liang.
idiomatic: Xiao Min, styled Renzu, was the son of Liang's Marquis Ye of Shanghuang.

literal: In the Tianbao era he entered [Northern] Qi; in Wuping he was crown prince groom.
idiomatic: In the Tianbao era he came into Qi; in Wuping he was crown prince groom.

literal: Gu Daozi was a man of Henei.
idiomatic: Gu Daozi came from Henei.

literal: His father Qi was Grand Master of Palace Counsel in Wei.
idiomatic: His father Qi had been grand master of palace counsel under Wei.

literal: Daozi had administrative talent; in office he was known for forceful execution, and passed through posts as reviewing censor and household-census retainer in the Minister of Works' fields bureau.
idiomatic: Daozi had real administrative grip; in office he was known for driving affairs through by force, and served as reviewing censor and household-census retainer in the Minister of Works' fields bureau.

literal: From Yuan Shuang downward, all had dipped into learning and possessed literary skill.
idiomatic: From Yuan Shuang on, all had touched learning and carried literary skill.

literal: Xun Zhongju and Xiao Min excelled at poetic composition.
idiomatic: Xun Zhongju and Xiao Min were masters of verse.

literal: Min once composed a poem on an autumn night; two of its lines ran, "Lotus dew falls away; willows thin out in the moon"—and connoisseurs prized them.
idiomatic: Min once wrote a poem on an autumn night whose two lines ran, "Lotus dew falls; willows thin in the moon"—and men of taste prized them.

literal: Praise: The nine currents and the hundred schools set words and establish virtue—without this pattern of culture, upon what would carving and inscribing rely?
idiomatic: Praise: The nine currents and the hundred schools set words and establish virtue—without this cultural pattern, what would carving and printing even serve?

literal: Yet the age fixes on decadent excess and forever speaks of beautiful norms—the elegant rectifies a state; the elegiac destroys one.
idiomatic: Yet the age dotes on lush excess and forever hymns beautiful norms: the elegant style rectifies a state; the elegiac style destroys one.

literal: The full text uses the Zhonghua Shuju first edition of the Book of Northern Qi (November 1972) as the base for collation.
idiomatic: The full text uses the Zhonghua Shuju first edition of the Book of Northern Qi (November 1972) as the base for collation.
